items.headline: AI stocks climb after trillions wiped from market values
items.blurb: Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat election victory would mean slower AI development.
items.text: Shares in artificial intelligence and technology firms have recovered slightly from an enormous sell-off that wiped trillions of dollars off stock values. The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock index closed in positive territory following a market rout that began in the US on Thursday before spilling over to Asian and European markets into Friday. Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat victory in the midterm elections would mean slower artificial intelligence development. However the latest US employment figures added to a mixed picture for American markets on Friday morning, with an unexpectedly strong 165,000 jobs added to the economy in September. On Thursday, businesses closely linked to artificial intelligence development took a hammering on stock markets, particularly chip and semiconductor makers. But the Nasdaq Composite bounced back slightly on Friday, ending the day up 1.1%, partly reversing some of its 5.5% fall. The S&P 500, which tracks the share prices of the largest publicly-traded US companies, closed up 0.3%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average was flat through the day before ending slightly down 0.4%.

items.headline: Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years for murder of 190 children
items.blurb: Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history.
items.text: Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history. The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa found the cult leader guilty of the crimes. Prosecutors said Paul Mackenzie and his Good News International church ran ​a Christian doomsday sect whose members were ordered to starve themselves and their children to death to go to heaven before the world ended. His accomplices threatened and beat victims to ensure they followed his orders. The emaciated bodies were found scattered in shallow graves and dumped in latrines. Some had been buried alive. Vice-President's JD Vance's reflection on where the midterms went wrong for Republicans has been interpreted as him paving the way for a 2028 run. items.text: Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80% of ballots counted. Wednesday’s fragmented vote marks another stage in the decline of the ANC, which has led national governments since the end of white minority apartheid rule in 1994. High unemployment, crime, corruption and poor local service delivery have all contributed to voters turning away from the party . The former liberation movement is projected to lose its status as the biggest party in the two most populous provinces, Gauteng and KwaZulu-Natal, as parties began coalition negotiations behind closed doors. The final results are expected to be announced on Sunday. The ANC was on 31.8% of the vote nationally, almost 14 percentage points below its 2021 local election result. items.headline: Two dead after bus crashes in France, officials say
items.blurb: One child and one young adult were killed in the crash, local authorities say, with more injured.
items.text: A young girl and an 18-year-old man have died after a bus crashed in eastern France, local authorities have said. The bus was travelling between Lyon and Bourg-en-Bresse when it crashed at around 07:00 local time on Friday in the town of Lent. The bus was carrying 43 passengers, including 15 children, the Bourg-en-Bresse prosecutor's office said. Three people are in a critical condition and at least 13 others have sustained minor injuries. French President Emmanuel Macron said his thoughts were with the victims, the injured, and their families. In a post on X, he said the nation stood by their side and thanked the rescue teams involved. The town's mayor Yves Cristin told French media the bus "left the road and hit a tree in the ditch". The two people killed have been identified by authorities. However, there have been differing reports as to the age of the girl. items.headline: Paraguay’s Santiago Pena under arrest, new president Pedro Alliana sworn in
items.blurb: The sudden leadership change comes as Paraguay reels from the collapse of the Ueno Bank, a popular lender.
items.text: Pedro Alliana has been sworn in as the new president of Paraguay, after a banking scandal led to the impeachment of his predecessor, Santiago Pena. On Friday, Alliana, 52, took the oath of office to become the South American country’s 53rd president. Previously, Alliana had served as vice president under Pena since the start of the latter’s term in 2023. But Pena’s tenure came to an abrupt end earlier in the day, after 44 of Paraguay’s senators voted to remove him from office. One senator in the 45-member chamber abstained. “I take my leave with gratitude, while fully acknowledging the anguish of those who are currently awaiting answers,” Pena wrote on social media on Friday afternoon. The impeachment marked a rapid fall from power for Pena, a member of the long-governing Colorado Party. His departure coincides this week with the sudden collapse of a prominent lending institution, Ueno Bank. Questions have arisen about whether the bank was properly regulated by government institutions, and whether Pena himself had conflicts of interest involving the bank. A humanitarian organisation sent the worker to DR Congo to help in the response to the outbreak, which is the second largest on record. items.headline: New wave of bomb threats hit European airlines
items.blurb: No link has been established between the threats against the airlines and those against the media outlets.
items.text: European airlines have again been hit with a new wave of bomb threats - in the third such incident this week. On Friday multiple flights to and from Lisbon, Rome, Prague and Sofia were targeted and the threats saw three planes escorted by Hungarian fighter jets, authorities said. It also saw a number of high-profile media organisations, including Ireland's public broadcaster RTÉ , evacuated after threats were made against them - although there has been no concrete links between the messages against airlines and the broadcasters. The disruption comes after nearly 30 aircraft and several airports across Europe were impacted by threats earlier this week , in what the UK called a "malicious hoax". A Ryanair flight scheduled to leave Lisbon for Rome on Friday was targeted with a threat, the airline said, while at least 11 flights were targeted in the Czech Republic and Bulgaria, according to AFP. India and the European Union have concluded negotiations on New Delhi’s association with a Euro 93.5 billion flagship research and innovation programme, paving the way for expanded collaboration under their broader strategic partnership. The decision comes weeks before India and the 27-nation bloc are set to seal a landmark free trade agreement — billed as the “mother of all deals” — to create a market of two billion people. The European Commission and India have successfully concluded negotiations on New Delhi’s association with the Horizon Europe programme, the EU said. This marks an important step forward for EU-India relations, strengthening scientific cooperation, creating new opportunities in research, and deepening the strategic partnership, it said. items.headline: Petrol pumps to check tanks for water ‘every 2–8 hours’: Officials
items.blurb: Experts said frequent testing with an alcohol-resistant water-finding paste is essential because ethanol readily absorbs water from its surroundings.
items.text: State-run oil marketing companies (OMCs) have decided that the over 93,000 petrol pumps nationwide will need to check their storage tanks and fuel dispensing nozzles for water every two to eight hours depending on shifts and weather conditions, to protect the quality of 20% ethanol-blended petrol (E20), persons aware of the matter said. The first such order passing on the decision for more frequent testing was issued in July, and another more recently in late October by one of the OMCs, according to people aware of the matter. The other two OMCs may follow suit, they added. It comes at a time when rains have lashed certain parts of the country. Most retail outlets (ROs) of Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) carry out these mandatory checks every two to four hours, the people cited above said, asking not to be named. Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) pumps have, however, reduced the frequency of testing to every eight hours. items.blurb: Indusekar, who also runs a Kannada-English monthly tabloid, allegedly confessed during interrogation, Bengaluru police commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh said.
items.text: A Bengaluru cab driver allegedly killed his wife and six of her relatives and dumped some of the bodies across Karnataka while his 11-year-old nephew, whose parents were among the dead, travelled with him believing they were on a holiday, police said on Friday. Indusekar alias Sekar , who also runs a Kannada-English monthly tabloid, allegedly confessed during interrogation, Bengaluru police commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh said. The victims were his wife Sunita, his mother-in-law Rupavathi, his brothers-in-law Shankar and Shivakumar, their wives Nalini and Divya, and Shivakumar and Divya’s seven-year-old son. Shankar and Nalini were the boy’s parents. “The accused claimed to have committed the murders over 15 to 20 days, a timeline that is still being verified,” Singh said. “He is giving a version that he called them one by one, murdered them, and disposed of the bodies in places he has indicated.” Police have recovered the child victim's body near Nandi Hills. “Six bodies are yet to be found,” Singh said. items.blurb: Anthropic's IPO valuation expectations have fallen sharply after a Wall Street sell-off, with investors now discussing a range of $1.2 trillion to $1.3 trillion, down from earlier expectations of up to $2 trillion.
items.text: Anthropic's ambitious initial public offering (IPO) plans are facing fresh valuation concerns after a sharp sell-off in US technology stocks, with prospective investors lowering their estimates of what the artificial intelligence company could be worth when it lists. Investors are now discussing a valuation of around $1.2 trillion to $1.3 trillion for Anthropic , with some considering a figure as low as $1.1 trillion, Bloomberg reported. The deliberations are ongoing and no final decisions have been made. The revised estimates mark a retreat from the $2 trillion valuation that Anthropic had reportedly been considering earlier. Even a valuation of $1.5 trillion is now facing resistance, with one investor describing that figure as a stretch, CNBC reported. According to CNBC , some investors now see a valuation of $1 trillion to $1.25 trillion as a more realistic target, although expectations could change depending on market conditions. The reassessment comes ahead of Anthropic's expected IPO roadshow next week. items.text: (Bloomberg) -- Losses at Arini Capital Management’s main hedge fund deepened in the final days of October, taking declines to 32% for the year, according to a letter to investors seen by Bloomberg. The high-yield debt specialist suffered a 19.7% loss in October alone as credit markets remained persistently weak, the letter said. Against that backdrop, the master fund run by Hamza Lemssouguer re-underwrote each of its five largest positions, representing about two-thirds of its net asset value. It also saw $389 million of inflows over the past week, part of its $1.5 billion raise. The fund “underestimated” the dislocation in CCC rated debt, which makes up the majority of the fund’s exposure, leading to a highly correlated portfolio, the letter said. items.text: Travel technology platform MakeMyTrip has acquired a majority stake in Bengaluru-based shared mobility startup Quick Ride, marking its entry into the ride pooling segment. The acquisition will expand MakeMyTrip’s ground transportation portfolio and strengthen its presence in daily urban commutes. Entrackr exclusively reported on October 19 that MakeMyTrip was in talks to acquire Quick Ride through its subsidiary redBus. However, the financial details of the transaction have not been disclosed. Founded in 2015 by KNM Rao, Quick Ride is an asset-light mobility platform that connects people travelling along similar routes for car and bike pooling. It enables users to share rides for everyday commutes and offers services to corporate employees through partnerships with companies, IT parks and business campuses. The platform aims to make commuting more affordable while reducing the number of vehicles on roads. According to MakeMyTrip, Quick Ride’s ride pooling business and brand have undergone an internal restructuring and are now housed under a new entity, Co Ride Mobility Private Limited. MakeMyTrip has acquired the brand and its ride pooling business through a majority stake in this entity.

items.text: Honasa Consumer, the parent company of Mamaearth, announced its financial results for the second quarter of the fiscal year ending March 2027. The company reported a 36% year-on-year growth in its revenue during the quarter, while its net profit surged 86.7% to Rs 73.25 crore. The Gurugram-based company's revenue from operations increased to Rs 731 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 538 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year, according to its financial statements accessed from the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE). The firm also recorded Rs 22 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 753 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 558 crore in Q2 FY26. On the expense front, the cost of materials consumed remained the largest expense component, increasing 38.4% to Rs 220 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 159 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. items.text: Google faced the ire of educators and parents earlier this week when it announced a new AI policy for K–12 schools . Google said that it developed its new approach to give schools more control, but early reporting also suggested Google would block search access for schools that didn’t want to use AI. Google didn’t see the backlash coming, but now that it’s here, the search giant is clarifying what exactly its new policy means and what’s changing. The gist of the new policy, according to Google’s blog post, is that schools using Google apps will have to opt into its AI products going forward. Since the company considers search part of its AI portfolio (Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Search), schools have to specifically turn that on for logged-in student accounts. items.headline: Securing the agentic enterprise with data lineage
items.blurb: A sales representative asks an AI agent for customer pricing, and the agent pulls data from multiple sources: restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes. The output looks accurate to the agent, so a second agent uses the data to draft the proposal for the sales rep.
items.text: A sales representative asks an AI agent for customer pricing, and the agent pulls data from multiple sources: restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes. The output looks accurate to the agent, so a second agent uses the data to draft the proposal for the sales rep. No human checks either handoff. When it’s discovered that the proposal includes unapproved, confidential, and sensitive information, no one can trace where the problematic data entered the workflow or how it spread across systems, files, and agents. This scenario illustrates why AI governance needs to evolve, rapidly and dynamically. As more enterprises begin to use agentic AI in daily workflows, they’re realizing that they must manage more than static files; they must manage moving and fragmented data that is continuously ingested, copied, summarized, transformed, reused, and redistributed in new forms. In short, AI security isn’t a tool problem; it’s a data visibility problem. Consequently, traditional security approaches built solely around applications, systems, networks, or endpoints are no longer sufficient. items.text: At the end of September, President Trump signed an executive order that contained just one directive, ordering government agencies to rebrand what they had been calling artificial intelligence as “Super Intelligence.” That term beat out other contenders, including “Extreme Intelligence” and “Supreme Intelligence,” offered by the president in a poll on X a couple of weeks earlier. Rebrands are, of course, now a White House tradition: Trump has changed names to project US dominance of certain bodies of water (the Gulf of America and Lake America), to signal new institutional priorities (Department of War), or simply to leave his mark on storied places (see the ongoing fight over renaming the Kennedy Center). The stated reason for this name change is that today’s AI systems “amplify human ingenuity” rather than merely “imitate” intelligence, and the government’s terminology should reflect that. One resource from a polling firm, called Redbud Consulting, tracked data center initiatives on the ballot and reported that out of 44 measures across 10 states seeking to restrict data centers, 38 passed so far. Those measures included dozens of moratoriums and bans. Analysts suggested those won’t impact data centers already under construction or approved through 2027, instead largely impacting future projects planned for 2028. Only one measure passed allowing a data center to proceed. But even that small win represented pushback on the AI industry—requiring data center developers in a North Dakota city to pay for independent reviews and hold public hearings when expanding or proposing projects. Companies are using more AI than ever, but they’re not spending more on it. A new report from Ramp shows AI spending flatlined over late summer even as token volumes rose, a sign that price competition and savvier customers may be capping revenue for OpenAI and Anthropic. According to Ramp’s data, token spend only grew 1.5% across August and September. To compare, in July, it grew 42% from the previous month.
